outcome: Low Apgar scores (below 7 at five minutes)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 33 pregnant mothers experiencing reduced fetal movements (RFM), primarily married women aged 18 to 29 years, at Port Sudan Maternity Hospital.
finding: The study found that reduced fetal movements (RFM) are frequently associated with serious adverse pregnancy outcomes, including low APGAR scores and intrauterine fetal demise (IUFD).
cross-section timing: Data was collected from February to August 2022 at Port Sudan Maternity Hospital.
birth_weight: 42.9% of newborns had birth weights between 2.5 kg and 3.5 kg.
gest_age: The first episode of RFM was commonly reported before 28 weeks of gestation (34.4%), and all stillbirths (12.1% of total births) were preterm babies.
